speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Given your history of AIDS, I need to assess the urgency and specifics of your vision loss. Can you describe when the symptoms started and if you have experienced any eye pain or headaches?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. Given your immune status and the painless nature of the vision loss, I am concerned about opportunistic infections like CMV retinitis or Toxoplasmosis. How long have you been on antiretroviral therapy, and do you know your most recent CD4 count?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Decreased vision and black spots in the right eye. I also have No pain, Left eye is asymptomatic.

speaker: Doctor
text: The painless nature of your symptoms combined with your history of AIDS strongly suggests Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis, which is the most common opportunistic eye infection in patients with low CD4 counts. I will now request a dilated fundus examination to look for characteristic hemorrhages and exudates, often described as "pizza pie" or "cottage cheese and ketchup" appearance. REQUEST TEST: Dilated_Fundus_Examination
